title: Do Hardwood Floors Need to Acclimate Before Installation? How Long in Kirkland?
meta: Solid hardwood needs 3 to 7 days to acclimate in a Kirkland home; engineered often needs 48 hours or less. Wills Flooring explains what really matters.
keywords: hardwood floor acclimation how long, do hardwood floors need to acclimate, acclimate engineered hardwood, hardwood installation Kirkland WA, wood floor moisture content before install
offers: Hardwood floor installation, engineered or solid

blocks.lead: Yes. Solid hardwood needs three to seven days in the room where it will be installed, engineered usually needs 48 to 72 hours, and both need the house running at normal living conditions the whole time.
blocks.detail: The calendar is only a guide. What we actually wait for is the wood's moisture content to land within a few percent of the subfloor's. In a Kirkland house in October that can take longer than the box says.

blocks.html: Ask this on a Kirkland remodel and you will hear everything from "two weeks minimum" to "just open the boxes." Both can be right for a specific product in a specific house. The problem is that most people treat acclimation as a number of days when it is really a moisture target. Below is how we handle it on Juanita, Rose Hill and Bridle Trails jobs, why lakefront houses are different, and how to keep it from wrecking your schedule.

items.title: Wood moves with moisture, not temperature
items.text: A hardwood board swells across its width as it takes on moisture and shrinks as it dries. Temperature by itself barely matters. Acclimation lets the boards reach the moisture level they will live at in your house, so the movement happens in the box, not in your floor.

items.title: The target is a gap, not a date
items.text: Industry practice for solid strip flooring is to install when the wood is within about 4 percent of the subfloor's moisture content, and within about 2 percent for wide plank. Engineered has its own manufacturer spec. We measure both with a pin meter and write the numbers on the quote.

items.title: The house has to be a house
items.text: Acclimating in a garage or a room with no heat is worse than not acclimating at all. The HVAC has to be running at the settings you will actually live with, ideally for a week before the wood arrives, so the subfloor is stable too.

items.title: Engineered is more forgiving, not immune
items.text: Cross-ply construction keeps engineered planks far more stable, and some manufacturers say sealed cartons need no acclimation at all. We still bring them inside 48 hours early. Kirkland deliveries in a rainy week arrive with the cartons colder and damper than the house.

blocks.text: Why Kirkland houses need a little more patience

blocks.html: Kirkland sits between the lake and the hills, and the two ends of town behave differently. A 1970s split-level in Finn Hill or Juanita, two blocks from the water and over a vented crawlspace, often reads 55 to 60 percent indoor humidity in October. A 2005 two-story in Bridle Trails with a sealed crawl and a modern furnace can sit at 38 percent the same week. The wood from the same pallet acclimates to two different numbers. That is why we meter the subfloor at the estimate, not on delivery day.

blocks.title: The over-acclimation trap:
blocks.text: Leaving solid hardwood for three weeks in a damp Kirkland house in November lets it swell before it goes down. Then the furnace runs all winter, the boards dry and shrink, and you get gaps in February. Longer is not safer. Matching the subfloor is safer, and if the house is running wet, fixing the humidity comes first.

blocks.text: How to keep acclimation from derailing your remodel

items.html: Order the wood before the painters finish. Delivery can land while other trades are still working, as long as the house is closed up and the HVAC is on. Just keep the cartons out of the paint room.
Set the thermostat to how you live, then leave it. Swinging between 60 at night and 74 during the day changes indoor humidity every cycle. A steady setting acclimates wood faster.
Ask for the meter readings in writing. Subfloor, room humidity and board moisture on install day. Any installer in Kirkland who will not give you those numbers is guessing.

Consider engineered for a tight timeline. If you are closing on a Houghton house and moving in ten days later, engineered gets you a finished floor with a two-day acclimation instead of a week. Our engineered vs solid post covers the tradeoffs.

faq.q: How long does hardwood need to acclimate before installation?
faq.a: Solid hardwood usually needs three to seven days inside the house at normal living conditions, longer for wide plank or damp homes. Engineered hardwood usually needs 48 to 72 hours. The real test is a moisture meter: the boards should be within about 2 to 4 percent of the subfloor before nailing.

faq.q: Can you install hardwood flooring the same day it is delivered?
faq.a: For most solid hardwood, no. For some engineered products in sealed cartons the manufacturer allows it, but we still prefer 48 hours indoors. In Kirkland the risk of same-day installation is cartons arriving cold and damp from a rainy delivery and then shrinking once the furnace dries them.

faq.q: Does engineered hardwood need to acclimate?
faq.a: Less than solid, but usually yes. The cross-ply core keeps engineered planks stable, so 48 to 72 hours in the room is typical. Check your product's installation sheet, because acclimating outside the manufacturer's stated method can void the warranty, and some brands ask for the cartons to stay sealed.

faq.q: What happens if hardwood floors are not acclimated?
faq.a: Boards installed too wet shrink after the first heating season and leave gaps. Boards installed too dry swell in fall humidity and cup or buckle against the walls. Either way the fix is expensive and the manufacturer can decline a warranty claim. Metering before installation avoids all of it.

faq.q: Where should hardwood be stored while it acclimates?
faq.a: In the rooms where it will be installed, stacked flat and off the subfloor, with the cartons opened or cross-stacked so air moves through them. Never in a garage, basement or unheated space. The house should be closed up with the heating or cooling running at normal settings.

faq.q: Does Kirkland's climate change how long wood floors acclimate?
faq.a: Somewhat. Homes near Lake Washington in Juanita, Houghton and Finn Hill run higher indoor humidity in fall and winter, which can stretch solid hardwood acclimation past a week. Newer, tighter homes in Bridle Trails or Rose Hill usually hit the target in a few days. The meter reading decides, not the neighborhood.
